title: Organic Food Prices Rising More than Other Food
paragraphs: Food prices have been rising for years, but organic food is becoming expensive even faster than regular food, according to a new analysis.

The analysis was carried out by LendingTree, a US financial services company, using data from the US Department of Agriculture. It found that prices for organic fruits and vegetables increased by 10% between January 2025 and January 2026. In comparison, the prices of conventional produce, which is grown without organic certification, rose by only 0.3% during the same period.
As a result, organic produce now costs much more than regular produce. On average, organic fruits and vegetables cost 59% more than their conventional versions.

Some organic products saw especially large price increases. The price of organic Roma tomatoes jumped by 186% compared with a year earlier, while organic green bell peppers rose by 117%. However, not all organic items became more expensive. Some, such as Gala apples, Honeycrisp apples and raspberries, actually became around a third cheaper.

There are several reasons why organic prices have been rising so quickly. Like other farmers, organic producers have faced higher costs because of inflation, and many have raised their prices to keep up with these expenses.

Despite the higher prices, Americans are still buying organic food. According to the Organic Trade Association, the US organic market grew three times faster than the total food market in 2025. It reached $76.6 billion, an increase of 6.8%.
Food prices in general have also risen sharply in recent years. According to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the cost of food bought to eat at home has increased by 26% since 2020.

Still, the results show that the price difference between organic and conventional food can vary greatly from one product to another, so the cost of choosing organic depends a lot on what shoppers put in their baskets.
